fragments.text: Dear colleagues, let me introduce my speech, which is entitled Coexistence of AI and Humanity. I'm Ivan Kotuliak from Slovak University of Technology, and in the same time, I am representative of Slovak Council of UNESCO, so I am responsible for information for all programs. I am a professor at the University in Computer Science. I've participated on more than 100 scientific papers and articles, and currently I'm cooperating with Slovak Republic on Quantum Strategy and Policies. Although I will do this speech, artificial intelligence is reshaping our society, so as we will learn a bit later, artificial intelligence is something which is today with us, so everybody from us is using artificial intelligence on daily basis, daily basis.

However, there are serious risks in using and deploying artificial intelligence, and therefore we have UNESCO's framework for inclusive and ethical and human-centered such-opt AI, and we in Slovakia are also advocating for balance between innovation and ethics. This balance is very important. We cannot just say that we will not focus anymore on research in the area, or we will not use any more the results of the research. However, we need to have this research balanced in the future. As I have told, AI is no longer a future concept. We use it in everyday life, and it's a reality. AI applications, we can know it, everywhere, education, health, governance, culture, and there are many and many fields which we

do not know yet, so it's growing into our daily life, and it is a serious impact, and it will have seriously impact in the future. However, there are huge discussions of transparency, accountability, and we need to manage how we will use, how we will deploy, how we will research artificial intelligence in the future. There are huge benefits, so I don't think we need to go through all of them, but let's take at least a couple of them, improvement of human life, and as efficiency, speech text, automatic translation, and many and many new opportunities. However, we do have a couple of risks. Bias and discrimination, surveillance and privacy, power, concentration in hands of a few

corporations. Bias and discrimination are known that research of AI is done in uncertain data. Data may be not well-equilibured for different cultures, different people, and therefore there can be a state-forward discrimination. Stay surveillance and privacy, so the question, where is still the democracy or individuality, and where starts privacy and where starts security of society? And this should be seriously discussed once more and all over the world. It's not the problem of some part of the world, it's a problem which comes all over the world. And power concentration in hands of a few corporations. There is something which is known today, so we have some huge companies like OpenAI, Google and others,

and there are only a couple of them, let's say worldwide, there are ten rather roughly ten of companies who concentrate this power in their form. What we should focus on in the future, it should be human-centric, so all AI development should be human-centric. It should not be some AI-centric or company-centric or something, the human and humanity individuality should be in the center of our focus. To achieve this goal, we need to focus on ethical principles, as was defined in UNESCO AI ethics recommendations, so from 2020-21, which includes fairness and non-discrimination, transparency and explainability and accountability. There is the dark side, I will focus more on the dark side and on the risk of deploying and using data.

Algorithmic coloniality, a new form of exploitation because there are certain regions, certain countries which are not able to build their own algorithms and they must buy and they have no other choice, so they can be exploited. No global north dominance, risk of imposing foreign values, so that's something which is important because we should advocate local culture and local languages development and not some global language or a global values enforcement in all the countries. Digital dependency is reinforced, can reinforce inequalities. As I will state later, we need to make choices, responsible choices, to develop our society. Algorithmic coloniality is something very important, so data, today data we can see as raw materials, so raw material which are mined from soil, so now the data we can see as new form of raw materials.

Without data you cannot train LLM, you cannot train new artificial intelligence, etc. And these data are usually concentrated in hands of a few companies which were already mentioned, and we need to open data to anybody who wants to train the data, who wants to develop new algorithms, etc. and should not be in hands of few companies or few states. Bices in design algorithms are trained on data reflecting the values and biases of their creators and that's something also which is impacting and homogenizing worldwide humanity, and this is not what we really should advocate for. We should advocate for local languages, for local culture, local communities. And then if we have these biases, we have imposed norms or platforms and technologies,

imposed cultural norms, political narratives, which we can see across the world. Information accessibility, so AI can reduce barriers, which is very advantageous, real-time translations, accessible content format, but it risks reinforcing division, if local contexts are ignored and this is done regularly, that we ignore local context. So we need to promote, as I've told, a couple of times already, linguistic, local, linguistic, cultural diversity. We need not, and we should not create digital filter bubbles, which was done with Facebook, with Instagram and other social networks, because it threatens the society, the existence of societies. Consistence of AI and humanity, AI should augment, not replace human decisions. So the coexistence of AI and humanity, as I've told, is a choice and we should advocate

this choice and we should select this choice as inevitable. It's not something which is by design and we should fight for it. Respect for identity, autonomy and creativity. We must choose the future where AI empowers, not exploits, and even we should advocate for the future where AI cannot create exploitation of any sort or any group of people and share this possibility between government, private sector or academia. So all the stakeholders should work together to build trustworthy and fair ethical AI. There are recommendations of support for open and transparent AI research, including data, promote local languages and culture, strengthen international cooperation, ensure inclusive policy and frameworks. So that's basically this. And the future outlook, we will not stop development of AI, so we need to hold these proposals.

As a conclusion, AI and humanity will coexist and it should be, AI should be human centric. They should coexist in mutual respect. There should be cooperation of all stakeholders to develop fair ethical AI. And my call to actions I like it very much is AI for all, not AI for you. Thank you.
